correctness.rationale: The edge-disk support sum is exact. Strict concavity on the squared-coordinate simplex follows from the absence of any nonzero solution of v_i+v_j=0 on all edges of a connected graph with a triangle. This proves symmetric optimizer uniqueness without assuming symmetry. Exact differentiation and Cauchy–Schwarz give the two radius branches, the complete contact set from h_K(u)=R iff Ru is a boundary contact, all antipodal diameters, and the C1/not-C2 quadratic branch-gap identity. The standalone checker passed 560 cases, 560560 scalar-grid checks, and 16800 full simplex samples. Finite tests do not substitute for the universal proof; no unproved step is used in the theorem.

value.rationale: This is the complete outer Euclidean radius, contact geometry and diametral pair classification of a natural family of high-dimensional Minkowski sums of genuinely two-dimensional disks. Under a continuous positive weight deformation, a fixed incidence structure undergoes a sharp second-order radius transition, a jump between 2^a and 2^(a+b) contact points, and square-root onset of previously screened coordinates. These are structural geometric boundaries, not a single arbitrary numerical evaluation.
